subject: Logic
title: Paradoxes Across Cultures
description: A fast breakdown of Paradoxes Across Cultures for builders.

hook.text: The Greeks had Zeno. China had the White Horse paradox. India had the Jain many-valued logic.

buildup.text: Every civilization that developed philosophy stumbled onto paradoxes. They seem to be universal.

discovery.text: Gongsun Long argued a white horse is not a horse—because "horse" doesn't specify color.

twist.text: Different cultures resolved paradoxes differently. Some embraced contradiction as part of reality.

climax.text: Paradoxes reveal not just logical limits but cultural attitudes toward truth and certainty.

punchline.text: Every culture finds where logic bends.

quiz.question: What did Gongsun Long's White Horse paradox argue?
options: A white horse is not a horse
